content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To protect grapes from insects, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Attach pheromone dispensers to the trellis (2 hours)
Step 2. Research local invasive beetle patterns (3 hours)
Step 3. Purchase fine-mesh fruit protection bags (1 hour)
Step 4. Apply organic neem oil spray (45 minutes)
Step 5. Inspect the vineyard perimeter for existing nests (2 hours)
Step 6. Install yellow sticky traps (30 minutes)
Step 7. Log the final inspection data (20 minutes)
Step 8. Order bird and insect netting in bulk (30 minutes)
Step 9. Mix a garlic and pepper repellent solution (40 minutes)
Step 10. Consult with an agricultural specialist (1 hour)
Step 11. Clear tall grass from around the vine trunks (3 hours)
Step 12. Prune excess foliage to improve airflow (4 hours)
Step 13. Secure the base of the protective bags with ties (1 minute)
Step 14. Calibrate the handheld sprayer (15 minutes)
Step 15. Tag the treated grape clusters (10 minutes)
Step 16. Inventory current pest control supplies (1 hour)
Step 17. Identify beneficial predatory insects in the area (2 hours)
Step 18. Remove fallen fruit from the ground (2 hours)
Step 19. Set up a weather monitoring station (1.5 hours)
Step 20. Release ladybugs into the canopy (30 minutes)
Step 21. Install motion-activated sprinklers (2 hours)
Step 22. Wrap the individual grape clusters (2 minutes)
Step 23. Construct a secondary physical barrier fence (5 hours)
Step 24. Perform a final walkthrough of the vineyard (1 hour)
Step 25. Check the integrity of the netting (30 minutes)
Step 26. Sort the mesh bags by size (30 minutes)
Step 27. Drive to the garden supply warehouse (45 minutes)
Step 28. Rinse the vines with a gentle water stream (1 hour)
Step 29. Label the different grape varieties (1 hour)
Step 30. Hang bird silhouette deterrents (1 hour)
Step 31. Distribute ant bait stations (45 minutes)
Step 32. Document the completion of the protective phase (30 minutes)
Step 33. Unroll the netting across the rows (2 hours)
Step 34. Sanitize the pruning shears (20 minutes)
Step 35. Inspect the vineyard for holes in the fencing (1.5 hours)
Step 36. Test the soil pH levels (30 minutes)
Step 37. Dig trenches for the fence posts (4 hours)
Step 38. Fasten the mesh bags over the grapes (3 hours)
Step 39. Sharpen the hedging tools (30 minutes)
Step 40. Recruit seasonal help for installation (4 hours)
Step 41. Create a seasonal pest management plan (2 hours)
Step 42. Map out the vineyard grid (2 hours)
Step 43. Purchase concentrated organic pesticides (1 hour)
Step 44. Install ultrasonic pest repellers (1 hour)
Step 45. Check the local agricultural forecast (10 minutes)
Step 46. Sterilize the work boots (15 minutes)
Step 47. Pick up the specialized insect tape (30 minutes)
Step 48. Apply a biological control agent to the soil (2 hours)
Step 49. Review the previous year's pest logs (1 hour)
Step 50. Post warning signs for the treated area (20 minutes)
Step 51. Fill the sprayer tanks (15 minutes)
Step 52. Spray the base of the vines (1 hour)
Step 53. Buy a high-pressure hose nozzle (15 minutes)
Step 54. Set up the ladder for high clusters (20 minutes)
Step 55. Clean the vineyard drainage ditches (3 hours)
Step 56. Mow the buffer zone between the field and woods (2 hours)
Step 57. Dispose of empty pesticide containers (30 minutes)
Step 58. Repair any tears found in the netting (1 hour)
Step 59. Drape the netting over the top of the vines (3 hours)
Step 60. Secure the netting edges to the ground (2 hours)
